item.title: We can't expect God to do all the work.
item.description: Hundreds of women marched to the courthouse carrying vegetable knives and chili powder, walked into the courtroom and took seats near the front. Akku walked in and was confident and unrepentant. When Akku appeared, he saw a woman he had raped. Akku mocked her, called her a prostitute and said he would rape her again. The police laughed. She told Akku either she would kill him or he would have to kill her saying, "We can't both live on this Earth together. It's you or me." The women passed their knives around and kept stabbing him; each woman agreed to stab Akku at least once. His blood was on the floors and walls of the courtroom. As he was being lynched, Akku was horrified and shouted: "Forgive me! I won't do it again!". Akku died 15 minutes later. The mob continued attacking his corpse post-mortem. All the women returned to to tell their husbands and fathers they had killed Akku. They celebrated, and families put on music and danced in the streets. They bought food and handed out fruit to their friends. Five women were arrested immediately but released following demonstrations in the city. Every woman living in the locality claimed responsibility for the lynching. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akku_Yadav

item.title: This is what's happening to Ukrainians when russia seizes their land.
item.description: On September 10, 2022, Ukraine liberated Izium after nearly six months of russian occupation. Investigators later exhumed 447 bodies: 425 civilians, including five children, and 22 Ukrainian servicemembers. Many had died violent deaths, while dozens showed signs of torture and execution. So when people suggest that Ukraine should surrender its territory to russia, they are talking about abandoning millions of Ukrainians to the same occupation, violence, torture and terror we have already witnessed. Russian officials have repeatedly made it clear that their idea of victory is not peace. It is the destruction of Ukraine as an independent nation.

item.title: God, Part 1
item.description: Our search for "god" is the search for purpose, happiness, and in a more metaphysical sense the search for using the spark or spirit we have as a tool for betterment. As a skeptic myself, I see our societies as products of people wanting to buikd a better life for one another, and sacrificing small parts of themselves to make the world better. It is the small steps like staying late to clean the places of worship, or spending extra time making that special meal for a loved one, perhaps giving up a night to care for someone sick, or an evening at a soup kitchen. Whatever we call it, religious, atheist, agnostic, skeptical or otherwise we TYPICALLY want "good."

item.title: GovBrief Today #591
item.description: Donald Trump's hand-picked board says the Kennedy Center goes broke unless his name goes back on the memorial. He took over the institution 18 days into his term. A judge ruled in May that Congress alone can rename it. Crews pried his name off in June, and a tarp has hidden the sign ever since. Now a 57-page packet tells the board the main building could close as soon as Tuesday and the center will miss payroll within weeks. Trump will only raise the money if the front of the building carries what the packet calls appropriate recognition. The vote comes two days before the judge hears whether the board’s last attempt to put his name up was legal. The board is not waiting for the ruling. item.title: God, Part 3
item.description: "Thou shalt have no other gods before me." To the religious this might mean to refuse idols, to the agnostic perhaps it means there are many gods, to the skeptic it still isnt proof of god. Even still, if god exists how can he be all good, and all powerful, and we still have freewill? There are too many paradoxes. Psychologically this is because we are making a victim and a victor, a god that will bring us vengeance when we are wronged and mercy when we wrong.
